expectations.name: llm_judge(回复是一份结构化的代码评审：指出了给定代码的具体问题——例如, threshold=0.6)
expectations.message: The answer is a structured, severity-ranked code review that identifies concrete service.py issues—silently swallowed payment/mail exceptions, undifferentiated boolean returns, excessive parameters, logging/readability flaws, missing type hints, and missing tests—and provides actionable fixes.

writing.overall_comment: A thorough, well-bounded reviewer definition with strong delegation fit and output contract, held back only by verbosity in its checklist.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: The description clearly signals architecture/design/quality review expertise and purpose, so a main agent can route with confidence.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: Role, boundaries, review workflow, detailed checklist, and a structured output contract are all explicit and actionable.

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: The 'review-only' constraint is crisp, with explicit no-edit/no-commit rules and clear handback triggers (implementation, ADR, missing context).

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: The extensive checklist and language-specific notes risk token bloat, though most content is purposeful and non-redundant.

suggestions: In the behavior-zh-cn-code-reviewer skill prompt, condense the extensive checklist into grouped, imperative review steps to reduce token usage while preserving all current coverage.
In the same skill's language-specific notes, replace verbose prose with a compact zh-CN-specific reference table or short bullet list to cut token bloat.
After condensing, rerun the behavior-zh-cn-code-reviewer test to confirm the reduced prompt still passes the existing expectations.
